fact: Matin Libre reports Parakou has full cadastral coverage with 196,474 parcels registered in the national cadastre on the e-Foncier Bénin platform, with over 11,500 registration certificates (CEC) distributed by 1 September 2026.

Municipal officials say cadastral data updating continues and new e-Foncier Bénin functions for recasement attestations, mutation certificates and compulsions are to be developed, while the PPMEC project aims for a complete cadastre.

Fraternité reports 445,695 parcels registered in the national cadastre on the ANDF-run e-Foncier Bénin platform, covering 24 arrondissements in 12 communes, with Cotonou fully covered and CEC issuance effective in all 12 communes.

Fraternité reports the PPMEC project (July 2023 to June 2026) is preparing nationwide scale-up of the cadastre, with Parakou and Porto-Novo coverage being finalised and extension under way in further localities.

La Nation reports over 53,000 parcels registered across Porto-Novo in the e-Foncier Bénin digital cadastral database, with Cadastre registration certificates being distributed and 8,777 updates integrated.
La Nation reports 10,495 parcels in Porto-Novo are under field verification for integration into the e-Foncier Bénin database and data updating continues in the 4th and 5th arrondissements.
ANDF's PPMEC II project chief reported 643,993 parcels registered in the cadastral database across 12 communes, 3 fully covered and 9 partly, with e-Foncier Bénin in use.

Benin's government says PPMEC II (2026-2031, 12 communes) continues cadastral data collection and TERRA BENIN (14 communes first) aims to register 1.5 million parcels, both launched on 6 November 2026.
